source.title: Rotary encodings recover absolute grid position in flattened 2D inputs (synthetic fixture paper)
source.text: We probe whether transformers trained on flattened 2D grids encode absolute cell position without any explicit coordinate features. Linear probes recover absolute row and column indices from mid-stack residual streams with 94.6% accuracy at sequence lengths up to 2048 tokens, and the probe accuracy is stable across three model scales. Ablating rotary encodings drops probe accuracy to 31.2%, indicating the position information is carried by the encoding rather than learned from grid content. In twenty-step rollouts the same models maintain cell identity without positional drift, with a mean coherence score of 0.91 against ground-truth trajectories.

proposals.claim: Transformers do recover absolute grid position from flattened inputs without explicit coordinate features, at sequence lengths above ours.
proposals.excerpt: Linear probes recover absolute row and column indices from mid-stack residual streams with 94.6% accuracy at sequence lengths up to 2048 tokens

proposals.claim: Positional coherence over twenty-step rollouts holds without explicit coordinate features.
proposals.excerpt: In twenty-step rollouts the same models maintain cell identity without positional drift, with a mean coherence score of 0.91

source.title: Byte-level tokenisation reduces training cost for code models (synthetic fixture paper)
source.text: We compare byte-level and subword tokenisation for code models at three scales. Byte-level training reduced wall-clock cost by 18% at equal downstream pass@1, and the gap widened with context length. We observe no change in reasoning benchmarks outside the code domain.
